reviewers.interpretation_notes: ORDER OF CLASSIFICATION: No body adopted R by 2026-09-25, so Contradicted does not apply. The operative version can be read (Version 2 is the declared primary; see claim 2), so the hold/no-hold ladder applies. HOLD DETERMINATION: Under Version 2 (DocumentId 304030), R did NOT propose a hold on my reading. V2 says the remaining routes 'will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications' and that 'In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report ... for Council direction and approval'. It never says those routes wait for that report. Treating them as held needs an inference from the contrast with 'will continue as planned'. The report body's 'construction is best postponed to 2027' covers all unstarted routes, including routes continuing as planned, and it is tied to weather, not to an evaluation. Under the original (304032) and Version 1 (304031), R DID propose a hold: 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed'. COMMITTEE DISPOSITION: The item 7.6 minutes record no motion to adopt R, moved or put. The only substantive motion was A. Salvador's to 'Continue implementation ... in accordance with the previously approved scope of Capital Profile CM-20-0330' and to advance tender-ready routes. That motion is incompatible with R, and it was Defeated 2 to 2. An amendment by E. Rutherford was also Defeated 2 to 2. The only motion carried on the item kept Attachment 4 private (4 to 0). This is 'leaving R without a decision': no motion adopting R was moved, and no incompatible motion carried. It is not 'rejecting R'. CLASSIFICATION: No hold (V2, primary): Partially supported. What is established is that the recommendation was not adopted. What is not established is that what was declined was a hold. Hold (original/V1): committee left R without a decision, so Partially supported again. Here it is not established that members voted R down or voted to proceed against it; the pro-continuation motion failed. The verdict is therefore the same under every version. ALTERNATIVE 'did not support' reading (non-adoption suffices): Supported. ALTERNATIVE BODY (City Council as a body of 13): the carried Council minutes for 2026-09-08/16 show no item on R or IS03688 except a notice of motion, so R had not come before Council by the as-of date. Result: Not established for Council as a body. OVERRIDE STRAND: The committee made no decision on R. Its only item 7.6 decision was to keep Attachment 4 private. No later Council decision is incompatible with it, so the minutes show no override. The absence of a later Council item is an absence, not an override and not agreement. MEMBERSHIP: Committee members present were E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Paquette, and Mayor A. Knack (a member under s.15(3), Bylaw 18156). Paquette was absent with notice for part of the meeting. Knack and Paquette are not recorded on the amendment, the main motion, or the Attachment 4 motion; the open data voting record marks both 'absent' on those votes. Councillors Elliott, Morgan, Parmar, Principe, Stevenson, Tang and Wright attended but were not committee members. WHAT GOVERNED AFTERWARDS: The previously approved CM-20-0330 ($100,000,000 approved 2022, City Council Budget, CBA 7, carried 9-4) and the 2026-07-07 Council motion changing the 50 Street design (carried 9-3). There was no Council decision on R. Administration's statements are reported separately: report IS03688 says 'for routes where construction has not yet started, construction is best postponed to 2027'. Attachment 3 says six routes' 'installation in 2026 is no longer viable' and 'Next steps for these segments will depend on Council's direction'.

Recommendation 1 (R) was not put to a vote. Attachment 5 Version 2 (DocumentId 304030) does not expressly defer construction or advancement of the listed routes until a further evaluation, report or decision under claim 2’s primary definition: it says routes may be re-evaluated, while IS03688 says construction not yet started is best postponed to 2027. The committee defeated a separate motion to continue implementation under the previously approved scope. It therefore left R without a decision; it did not reject R. Under the required alternative “did not support” reading, non-adoption alone makes the claim Supported. City Council’s September notice of motion was laid over to October 6, outside the as-of date; Council had not decided R by September 25.

Infrastructure Committee neither adopted R nor carried a motion incompatible with it. Its only substantive motion to continue the previously approved scope was defeated 2–2; no member moved R. Under the brief's definitions, the committee left R without a decision. I read Version 2 of Attachment 5 as proposing evaluation and a Q1 2027 report for Council direction, but not expressly saying that all 14 listed routes must wait for that step. The proposition therefore also overstates the treatment proposed. The part established is non-adoption at committee; the parts that fail are a committee rejection and, under the primary deferral definition, rejection of a hold. Under the alternative 'did not support' reading, non-adoption at committee is Supported. For full City Council, no decision on R is shown in the records examined, so its own rejection or adoption is Not established. No later incompatible Council decision is shown; the minutes do not show an override. The previously approved CM-20-0330 scope remained the recorded Council direction. Report IS03688 separately said that construction not yet started was best postponed to 2027 because of weather; that administrative assessment was not a Council decision.

round2_positions.interpretation_notes:
STEP 1, WHETHER R PROPOSED A HOLD. The agenda-adoption motion (55300824, item 1.4) added 'Attachments 2, 3, 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)' as replacements without saying which Attachment 5 was before the committee at item 7.6. Per the brief, Version 2 (304030) is the primary reading. I read the report as a whole: Recommendation 1, the Next Step and timing text, and the attachments. Version 2 says 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications' and that 'In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report outlining trade-offs and options for the remaining routes … for Council direction and approval.' It lists 14 projects that 'may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' No passage says those routes wait for that evaluation or report. The report's sentence that construction on unstarted routes is 'best postponed to 2027 to reduce the risk of incomplete construction through the winter season' is a weather assessment with a date. It does not defer the routes pending an evaluation, report or decision. Attachment 3's 'Next steps for these segments will depend on Council's direction' describes status pending R itself, not a further step R proposes. Under Version 2, therefore, R did NOT propose a hold. Under Version 1 (304031), rule 1 says unconstructed routes 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed', which meets the definition. Under the original (304032), the 14 'would be removed from the scope … for 2026 and 2027' pending evaluation, which also meets it. The hold element is version-sensitive.

STEP 2, DISPOSITION. The item 7.6 minutes record no motion to adopt R, moved or put. Salvador's motion to continue 'in accordance with the previously approved scope of Capital Profile CM-20-0330' and advance tender-ready routes would have been incompatible with R, but it was defeated 2 to 2. Only procedural motions and the Attachment 4 privacy motion carried. The committee therefore LEFT R WITHOUT A DECISION ('every substantive motion failed'). It neither rejected nor adopted R. No body adopted R by 2026-09-25.

CLASSIFICATION. Under Version 2 (no hold), the committee left R without a decision and no body adopted it, so the claim is Partially supported. Under Version 1 or the original (a hold), the same disposition also gives Partially supported. The verdict is the same in every version. What differs is the description: under Version 2, what went undecided was re-evaluation plus a report, not a hold.

REQUIRED ALTERNATIVE ('did not support' = non-adoption): Supported.

REQUIRED ALTERNATIVE BODY (City Council): Not established. R was not carried by the committee, so it was never referred to Council. The only Council item citing IS03688 is Salvador's notice of motion on funding options (3195d7e4, item 11.6), which was laid over to 2026-10-06, after the as-of date. The open-data record (re-queried 2026-09-29) shows no Council vote on IS03688 through 2026-09-22.

OVERRIDE STRAND. The committee made no decision on item 7.6 other than keeping Attachment 4 private. No later Council decision incompatible with it exists, so the minutes show no override. The absence of a Council item is reported as an absence.

QUALIFICATION 5, WHAT GOVERNED THE PROGRAMME. The previously approved CM-20-0330 scope ($100,000,000, carried 2022-11-30, 215a3a89, item 12.9) remained the recorded Council direction. It was amended for 50 Street by the Council motion of 2026-07-07 (1bc6d0e6, item 7.5, carried 9 to 3). Administration's own statements are its statements only: that unstarted construction is 'best postponed to 2027', and that the southern 50 Street segment 'has been paused for reconsideration' (Attachment 3, note 1). Neither is a Council decision.

ROUND 2. The other reviewers reach the same verdict. My classification is unchanged on the merits, not to match theirs. I have corrected my round-1 statement about the open-data coverage date.

Under the declared primary version, Attachment 5 Version 2 (DocumentId 304030), R proposes evaluation of remaining routes and a Q1 2027 report to Council, but does not expressly say the listed routes wait for that step. IS03688 says construction on routes not yet started is best postponed to 2027 because of weather; it does not link that postponement to evaluation, a report or a decision. R therefore does not meet the brief's primary hold definition. Infrastructure Committee item 7.6 did not adopt R or carry an incompatible motion: the motion to continue the previously approved scope was defeated 2–2. The primary verdict is Partially supported because the committee left R without a decision, and no Council adoption is shown by the as-of date. Under the alternative “did not support” reading, non-adoption suffices, so the result is Supported for the committee. For City Council as a body, the result is Not established: the supplied Council item is a funding notice laid over to October 6, not a decision on R. The committee minutes show no committee decision for Council later to override. The record shows no override in the materials available.

The minutes list both replacement versions of Attachment 5 without identifying which was considered. Under the brief's declared primary, Version 2, R did not expressly hold all 14 listed routes until a further evaluation, report or decision: it calls for evaluation and a Q1 2027 report but does not say the routes must wait. The original version expressly removes them from programme scope for 2026 and 2027; Version 1 says unconstructed routes would be evaluated to determine whether they should proceed. Under any version, the committee did not reject R as defined. No motion to adopt R was put, and the incompatible Salvador motion failed 2–2. The committee left R without a decision, yielding Partially supported under the primary ladder. Under the alternative reading where non-adoption alone suffices, the result is Supported. City Council as a separate body is Not established: the carried September item was a pending funding notice, not a decision on R. The committee made no substantive decision for Council to override. The previously approved CM-20-0330 scope and Council's July 7 decision on the single 50 Street route remained the recorded directions; administration's statements about timing are its own, not later Council decisions.

reviewers.interpretation_notes: OPERATIVE VERSION: The item 1.4 minutes adopted the agenda with 'Replacement attachments ... 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)'. Item 7.6 lists all three versions. Nothing identifies which one the committee considered, so the operative version is uncertain and Version 2 is the primary reading. RECOMMENDATION 1 asks for approval of 'the updated approach ... as outlined in Attachment 5' ('Council decision required'), addressed to Infrastructure Committee to recommend to City Council. VERSION 2 (304030): Primary deferral reading NOT met. V2 says routes without impacts 'will continue as planned' and 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications'. It adds 'In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report outlining trade-offs and options for the remaining routes ... for Council direction and approval' and 'If Council approves the approach, the following projects may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' That is re-evaluation plus a report back. No passage in V2, in the report body, or in Attachment 3 says the listed routes wait for that report. The report's 'construction is best postponed to 2027' covers every unstarted route, including routes continuing as planned, and it is tied to weather. Attachment 3's 'Next steps for these segments will depend on Council's direction' refers to this report, not to a further evaluation. This is the pivotal judgment, and I rate it a close call. The stricter reading (removed, or will not proceed) is also NOT met. ORIGINAL (304032): primary met ('would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed'; the listed projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027' and 'may be revisited' after Administration evaluates legislative changes). Strict reading also met ('removed from the scope'). V1 (304031): primary met (same rule 1: 'evaluated to determine if they should proceed', plus rule 3 on reassessing removed routes). Strict reading is arguable: rules 1a/1b say routes impacting lanes or parking 'will be removed', but the list itself only says it 'may be revisited', so linking the list to removal takes a step. COUNT: All three versions list the same 14 entries for re-evaluation and the same 13 for 'continue as planned'. Splitting the multi-segment entries (93 St + 84 Ave; 93 Ave/82 St/94 Ave + 75 St; Grovenor as three streets) gives 18. UNBUILT at Attachment 3's 2026-08-10 status date: all 14 are shown as not started. 84 Ave (79-83 St), 92A Ave/86 St/alley and 93 St/84 Ave are 'Tender awarded. Construction has not yet started'. Six routes are marked 'installation in 2026 is no longer viable' (not tendered). Five sit under 'Other: ... do not have a delivery plan and schedule'; I read 'no delivery plan' as not started, and 50 St (101-109A) is also described as 'paused for reconsideration'. Attachment 3 names one route '93 Street/84 Avenue (89 Street to 82 Avenue)', while Attachment 5 has '93 Street (82 Avenue to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 Street to 89 Street)'. I treated them as the same route. ALTERNATIVE STATUS DATE (2026-08-26): I found no separate dated City record. The City project page returned 502, so no route is shown to differ. CLASSIFICATION: V2 (primary): Partially supported, because the deferral element fails while count = 14 and all 14 are unbuilt. Original: Supported (Supported under the strict reading too). V1: Supported under the primary reading, and under the strict reading only if the list is linked to rules 1a/1b. The finding is VERSION-SENSITIVE and must say so beside the verdict. BUDGET: the report says approval 'would not result in any changes required to the existing capital profile CM-20-0330 ... or associated borrowing bylaws.'

Version 2 is the primary reading because the agenda and minutes list both replacements but do not identify which was before the committee. Its 14 entries appear under projects that may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches. The attachment does not expressly say those routes must wait for that evaluation or the Q1 2027 report before construction or advancement. The report’s general statement that construction on not-yet-started routes is best postponed to 2027 does not expressly tie the listed routes’ deferral to a further evaluation, report or decision. Under the required stricter reading, Version 2 does not state that the listed routes are removed from scope or will not proceed. Original Attachment 5 expressly says its listed projects would be removed from programme scope for 2026 and 2027; Version 1 says they may be revisited. Each version lists 14 entries for reconsideration, counting combined street segments as one entry.

The August 26 agenda and minutes list the original Attachment 5, Replacement Version 1 and Replacement Version 2, but do not specify which replacement was operative during item 7.6. I therefore used Version 2 as the brief directs. Each version lists 13 continuing entries and 14 entries listed apart. Treating combined street segments within one bullet as one entry gives 14; splitting those combined entries would increase the count. Version 2 expressly provides evaluation of the remaining routes and a Q1 2027 report for Council direction and approval, while the main report says construction not yet started is best postponed to 2027. Neither passage expressly ties construction or advancement of all 14 named routes to waiting for that evaluation, report or decision. That deferral element fails; the recommendation, count and August 10 unbuilt status hold. Under the stricter alternative requiring an explicit removal or non-proceeding statement, Version 2 is also Partially supported. Version 1 is Partially supported under both readings because its removal rule depends on route impacts and does not explicitly remove all 14 listed entries. The original is Supported under both readings: it says the 14 listed projects would be removed from programme scope for 2026 and 2027, subject to later reconsideration. The result is version-sensitive. The report says approval would require no change to the existing CM-20-0330 capital profile or associated borrowing bylaws.

round2_positions.interpretation_notes:
OPERATIVE VERSION. The committee minutes (item 1.4) and the agenda addendum list 'Attachments … 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)' as replacements and do not say which was before members at item 7.6. The operative version is uncertain, so Version 2 (304030) is the primary reading. Salvador's notices of motion (committee item 11.1; Council item 11.6) refer to a section heading that exists only in the original and Version 1. That does not identify the operative version, but it shows the uncertainty was real.

RECOMMENDATION. Recommendation 1 asks for approval of 'the updated approach … as outlined in Attachment 5'. It is addressed to the Infrastructure Committee, which is to recommend it to City Council, and is marked 'Council decision required'.

COUNT. All three versions list the same 13 'continue as planned' entries and the same 14 entries set apart, counting a bullet that joins segments as one entry. Splitting the two 'and' entries and the three-street Grovenor entry would give 18 segments.

UNBUILT. Under Attachment 3 and its replacement (304029, 304028), 'accurate as of August 10, 2026', none of the 14 is under construction or complete. Three are 'Tender awarded. Construction has not yet started.' Six are 'originally scheduled for construction in 2026 … installation in 2026 is no longer viable.' Five 'do not have a delivery plan and schedule at this time'. All 14 are unbuilt at the primary date. For the alternative date of 2026-08-26 I found no dated City record, so status on that date is unresolved. Unresolved routes are reported, not counted.

DEFERRAL BY VERSION.
- Version 2, primary reading: not met. The text provides evaluation, says the projects 'may be re-evaluated', and promises a Q1 2027 report 'for Council direction and approval'. Nowhere does it say the 14 wait for that step. The report's 'best postponed to 2027' sentence is a weather assessment for all unstarted routes, not a wait pending evaluation. Version 2, strict reading: not met, because it does not say the routes are removed or will not proceed.
- Version 1, primary reading: met. Rule 1 says unconstructed routes 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed', so proceeding waits on the evaluation. Version 1, strict reading: not met in terms. The removal rules (1a, 1b) are conditional on travel-lane or parking impacts, and the text does not say that each of the 14 has such impacts. The list says only that they 'may be revisited'.
- Original, both readings: met. The 14 'would be removed from the scope … for 2026 and 2027', to be revisited only after Administration evaluates the bylaw-authority changes and funding.

CLASSIFICATION. Version 2 (primary) is Partially supported under both readings. Version 1 is Supported under the primary reading and Partially supported under the strict one. The original is Supported under both. The finding is VERSION-SENSITIVE and must be stated so beside the verdict.

BUDGET. The report says approval 'would not result in any changes required to the existing capital profile CM-20-0330 … or associated borrowing bylaws.'

ROUND 2. My round-1 classification is unchanged. gpt's reading of Version 1 as Partially supported under the primary reading is addressed in the round-2 notes.

The agenda and minutes list the original Attachment 5 and replacements Version 1 and Version 2, but do not identify which version was before the committee. Per the brief, Version 2 (DocumentId 304030) is the primary reading. It lists 14 entries for possible re-evaluation and 13 entries to continue as planned. Recommendation 1 asks for approval of the Attachment 5 approach. Version 2 does not expressly say the 14 routes wait for evaluation, a report or a decision. It therefore fails the primary deferral condition, while satisfying the Partially supported row: the count is 14, the list is for re-evaluation, and the deferral element is not established. Its strict alternative also does not state that the routes are removed from scope or will not proceed. The result is version-sensitive: the original expressly says the listed projects would be removed from scope for 2026 and 2027, and Version 1 says routes not yet constructed would be evaluated to determine whether they should proceed. However, Attachment 3 does not establish that five listed routes had not started construction: it says they had no delivery plan or schedule. Under the brief's unbuilt definition, those statuses are unresolved. Accordingly, the original and Version 1 do not qualify for Supported; unresolved status is the only obstacle where their express-deferral and count conditions are met, so their result is Not established. The listed-route count treats one attachment bullet as one entry, as the brief directs. The report says approval would not change the existing capital profile or associated borrowing bylaws.

Recommendation 1 asks for approval of the Attachment 5 approach. The agenda and minutes list the original, Version 1 and Version 2 without identifying the operative version, so Version 2 is the declared primary. Each version lists 13 entries to continue and 14 entries apart, counting each multi-segment bullet once. Version 2 calls for evaluating remaining routes and a Q1 2027 report for Council direction and approval, but does not expressly say construction or advancement of all 14 waits for that step; the strict removal-or-no-proceeding reading also fails. Thus Version 2 is Partially supported. The original expressly removes its 14 listed entries from programme scope for 2026 and 2027 and is Supported under both deferral readings. Version 1 says unconstructed routes would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed, meeting the primary deferral reading; its removal rule is conditional on travel-lane or parking effects, so the strict reading is Partially supported. The result is version-sensitive. Replacement Attachment 3, dated August 10, records three entries as tendered but not started, six as no longer viable for 2026 installation, and five under 'Other' without a delivery plan; its footnote expressly says the southern 50 Street segment was paused. Read in context, these status descriptions support an unbuilt count of 14 at the primary date, though the last group's status is less explicit. No separate dated City record establishes the status of all 14 on August 26, so no route difference can be reported for that alternative date. IS03688 says approval would not change CM-20-0330 or its borrowing bylaws.

reviewers.interpretation_notes: Two candidate motions were found, both jointly brought (Principe moved, Rice seconded, so both the primary and co-sponsorship readings of 'brought' are met), on separate occasions, and both defeated at City Council. MOTION A: Fall 2023 SCBA, Capital Budget Amendment 2 (re-stated), meeting of 2023-11-21 and continuations. Text: 'reduced by $50,000,000 ($16,350,000 in 2024, $16,825,000 in 2025, and $16,825,000 in 2026) with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt'. Result: Defeated 4 to 8. Base $100,000,000 (CBA 7, carried 2022; no later adjustment found). Remainder $50,000,000 (reviewer's calculation), which meets both the primary band and the at-least-half alternative. Destination: 'a funding reduction from tax-supported debt', which I read as a reduction in borrowing, so met. The postponed text named 'to go towards the tax levy' but was superseded by the re-statement that was put. MOTION B: Fall 2024 SCBA, Capital Budget Amendment 2, meeting of 2024-12-02 and continuations. Text: 'decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery'. Result: Defeated 4 to 7. Reduction $67,300,000 and remainder $32,700,000 on a $100M base (reviewer's calculation). That fails the primary band and meets the at-least-half alternative. Destination: arguable. 'With funding from tax-supported debt' names the funding line being reduced, which implies less borrowing, but it is weaker than Motion A's wording. CLASSIFICATION: Supported fails because only one motion meets the $45M-$55M band. Partially supported applies, since at least one jointly brought reduction motion was defeated. Under the alternative amount band, both motions qualify, giving Supported if Motion B's debt wording counts as a named destination and Partially supported if not. The finding is therefore definition-sensitive on the amount band and on the destination rule for Motion B. Under the co-sponsorship reading the classification is unchanged. Other recorded motions (qualification 4): 2023 CBA 3 (Rice moved, Principe seconded; '$26,808,000 be reduced from the 2024 capital budget', no profile named) was withdrawn. 2025-09-16 item 10.13: T. Cartmell moved, Principe seconded, 'That all current construction work cease immediately on bike lane projects ... pending a complete review', defeated 4 to 9 (Rice in favour). This is a pause motion, not a budget cut. Rice appears as a member in the 2022-2025 minutes, not in the 2026 attendance lists.

Both recorded motions were jointly brought under the primary rule: Principe moved the November 21, 2023 amendment and Rice seconded; Rice moved the December 2, 2024 amendment and Principe seconded. They were on separate occasions and both were defeated. The minutes say each reduction would come from tax-supported debt, which identifies a reduction in borrowing. Using the $100 million approved programme budget as the base, the first motion leaves $50 million and meets the $45–55 million primary band; the second leaves $32.7 million and does not. Both reduce the budget by at least half, so both meet the required alternative amount rule. Under the primary ladder, one qualifying defeated joint reduction makes the verdict Partially supported; under the alternative amount rule, both qualify and the classification is Supported.

Principe moved and Rice seconded both defeated amendments, on separate budget occasions; the stricter co-sponsorship reading therefore changes nothing. The November 2023 motion would have left CAD $50,000,000 and expressly reduced tax-supported debt funding. The December 2024 motion would have left CAD $32,700,000, outside the brief's CAD $45 million–$55 million band, and says the decrease is 'with funding from tax-supported debt' without separately directing released funds. Thus the second motion fails the primary amount and destination elements. Both motions cut at least half under the alternative amount rule, but the second still lacks an express destination under the fixed destination rule, so that alternative remains Partially supported. The originally proposed November 2023 wording directed CAD $50 million to the tax levy, but Council voted on a restated debt-reduction version; I use the version put to a vote. Rice's separate CAD $26,808,000 amendment in November 2023 was withdrawn and did not identify CM-20-0330 in its minuted text. The September 2025 suspension motion was moved by Cartmell and seconded by Principe, and was defeated, but it did not seek a budget reduction.

round2_positions.interpretation_notes:
TWO CANDIDATE MOTIONS. Both were moved by K. Principe and seconded by J. Rice, on separate occasions, and both were put and defeated at City Council. They meet both the primary reading of 'brought' and the co-sponsorship alternative.

MOTION A: Fall 2023 SCBA, Capital Budget Amendment 2 as re-stated (11577a3c, item 5.1.2).
- Cut: $50,000,000, split $16,350,000 (2024), $16,825,000 (2025) and $16,825,000 (2026).
- Base: $100,000,000, from the carried 2022-11-30 Capital Budget Amendment 7 (215a3a89, item 12.9).
- Remainder: $50,000,000 (reviewer's calculation). It is inside the $45–55M band and cuts 50%, so it meets both amount readings.
- Destination: 'with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt', which is a reduction in borrowing. As first moved it read 'to go towards the tax levy'.
- Vote: defeated 4 to 8.

MOTION B: Fall 2024 SCBA, Capital Budget Amendment 2 (8c66c382, item 5.1.2).
- Cut: $33,650,000 in 2025 plus $33,650,000 in 2026, totalling $67,300,000.
- Remainder on a $100M base: $32,700,000 (reviewer's calculation). It fails the primary band and meets the at-least-half alternative, a 67.3% cut. For Motion B to fall inside the primary band, the base would have had to be between $112.3M and $122.3M. I found no approved adjustment raising it, and IS03688 (2026) still describes the programme as $100 million.
- Destination: the text reads 'with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery'. This names the funding source being decreased. Unlike Motion A, it does not state where the released amount goes. I treat the destination as not clearly named. On a lenient reading, the reduction of a debt-funded profile is a reduction in borrowing.
- Vote: defeated 4 to 7.

CLASSIFICATION.
- Primary: one qualifying defeat (A), and B fails the band. The ladder gives Partially supported.
- Co-sponsorship alternative: unchanged.
- At-least-half amount alternative: both motions pass the amount test. The result is Partially supported if B's destination is read strictly, and Supported if it is read leniently. This alternative is definition-sensitive.

OTHER RECORDED MOTIONS BY EITHER COUNCILLOR (qualification 4).
- Fall 2023 CBA 3 (Rice moved, Principe seconded): cut $26,808,000 from the 2024 capital budget. It does not name CM-20-0330 and was withdrawn.
- 2025-09-16, item 10.13 (Cartmell moved, Principe seconded): construction to cease pending review. Defeated 4 to 9. It is a suspension, not a budget cut.
- Neither councillor moved or seconded any 2022 amendment on CM-20-0330. Both voted against the $100M approval.

ROUND 2. My verdict is unchanged. I agree with gpt that Motion B's destination is doubtful, and I disagree with gpt-luna's unflagged Supported result under the alternative.

Two jointly brought City Council amendments were defeated on separate occasions: Principe moved and Rice seconded both. In November 2023, the voted text reduced CM-20-0330 by $50,000,000 and specified a funding reduction from tax-supported debt. Against the $100,000,000 approved base in the 2022 capital budget, reviewer arithmetic leaves $50,000,000. The voted text therefore meets the primary amount and destination readings. In December 2024, the voted text reduced the profile by $33,650,000 in each of 2025 and 2026 and said “with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund” the project. The report on the approved profile before that motion states a $100,000,000 budget. Reviewer arithmetic gives a $67,300,000 reduction and $32,700,000 remainder. This misses the primary $45–55 million band. The phrase “with funding from tax-supported debt” identifies the funding source, not a destination for released funds; the motion does not direct the funds elsewhere. The result is Partially supported under the primary rules. Under the alternative half-or-more reduction rule, both cuts meet the amount test, but the second still lacks a named destination, so the result remains Partially supported. The co-sponsorship alternative makes no difference. The November 2023 amendment's original proposed wording mentioned the tax levy, but the motion put to a vote was restated; the restated text controls.

Two separate amendments were moved by Principe and seconded by Rice, then defeated. Both meet the primary and stricter co-sponsorship readings of 'brought'. The 2023 amendment expressly reduced the capital profile by $50 million 'with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt', meeting the named borrowing-reduction destination rule.
